question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

These include the nature/ documentaries, including/ The Blue Planet and Planet Earth.
option_2: The Blue Planet and Planet Earth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every segment of the sentence is grammatically sound, so the answer is No error. (कोई त्रुटि नहीं)

◦ "These include the nature" — the plural subject "These" correctly takes the plural verb include, and "the nature" is a valid noun phrase here.

◦ "documentaries, including" — the participle including properly introduces the examples that follow.

◦ Correct: These include the nature documentaries, including The Blue Planet and Planet Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is not the error segment — "including" is the standard way to list examples after a noun.

• Option 2 is not the error segment — titles of programmes are correctly capitalised.

• Option 4 is not the error segment — subject–verb agreement (These – include) is correct.

NOTE

• In SSC error-spotting, always check first for subject–verb agreement, tense, preposition, article and parallelism; if all four are clean, "No error" is the answer.

• "Including" is never followed by "of": *including the states* (✓), *including of the states* (✗).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

A long hoped-for revival in private investment has not take place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. not take place.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the present perfect tense — "has" must be followed by the past participle (V3), not the base form V1. (पूर्ण वर्तमान काल)

◦ Structure: has/have + V3. So "has not take" must become has not taken.

◦ Correct: A long hoped-for revival in private investment has not taken place.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A long hoped-for revival" is correct — "hoped-for" is a properly hyphenated compound adjective before the noun.

• Option 4 "in private investment has" is correct — the singular subject "revival" takes the singular auxiliary "has".

• Option 3 is wrong because the sentence clearly does contain a verb-form error.

NOTE

• V1–V2–V3 of common irregulars: take–took–taken, give–gave–given, write–wrote–written, break–broke–broken.

• "Take place" = to happen (a fixed collocation); it has no passive form.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Still, this is a Frank Black album, with its ______ references and abstruse lyrics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. obscure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Obscure means not clearly understood, hard to make out, little known. (अस्पष्ट / गूढ़)

◦ The blank is joined by "and" to abstruse lyrics; "abstruse" means difficult to understand, so the parallel adjective must carry the same sense — obscure.

◦ Correct: Still, this is a Frank Black album, with its obscure references and abstruse lyrics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "intelligent" (बुद्धिमान) describes a person's mental ability and does not parallel "abstruse".

• Option 3 "informal" (अनौपचारिक) refers to a casual style, unrelated to difficulty of meaning.

• Option 4 "apparent" (स्पष्ट) means obvious — the exact opposite of "abstruse", breaking the parallelism.

NOTE

• Synonyms of obscure: vague, cryptic, ambiguous, enigmatic, unclear.

• Antonyms of obscure: clear, evident, manifest, lucid, transparent.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Be present ______ the moment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is in the moment, meaning fully attentive to the present. (वर्तमान में रहना)

◦ The preposition in is used with periods of time viewed as an enclosing whole — *in the morning, in 2023, in the moment*.

◦ Correct: Be present in the moment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to the moment" is not an English collocation; "to" indicates direction or a recipient.

• Option 2 "upon the moment" is unidiomatic — "upon" suits phrases like *once upon a time*.

• Option 3 "on the moment" is wrong; "on" is used with days and dates — *on Monday, on 5 June*.

NOTE

• Time prepositions: at (exact time — at 6 p.m.), on (days/dates), in (months, years, longer periods).

• Related idioms: at the moment (right now), for the moment (for the time being), in a moment (very soon).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Complicate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Enlighten.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Complicate means to make something more difficult, confused or involved. (जटिल बनाना)

◦ Enlighten means to give someone clarity or understanding — to make a matter clear. (समझाना / प्रबुद्ध करना) It therefore opposes "complicate".

◦ Correct: Rather than complicate the issue, the teacher chose to enlighten the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Multiply" (गुणा करना / बढ़ना) means to increase in number — not an opposite of complicate.

• Option 2 "Dominate" (प्रभुत्व जमाना) means to control or rule over.

• Option 3 "Healthy" (स्वस्थ) is an adjective describing good health, so it cannot be the antonym of a verb.

NOTE

• Synonyms of complicate: confuse, muddle, entangle, convolute.

• Other antonyms of complicate: simplify, clarify, streamline, unravel, elucidate.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hit the hay
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To go to bed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom hit the hay (also hit the sack) means to go to bed / go to sleep. (सोने जाना)

◦ It comes from the days when mattresses were stuffed with hay or straw.

◦ Correct: It's past midnight — I'm going to hit the hay.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To buy or sell something" is the sense of idioms like *strike a deal*, not "hit the hay".

• Option 3 "To take revenge" corresponds to *pay someone back / settle a score*.

• Option 4 "A sarcastic response" describes tone, not this idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Related sleep idioms: hit the sack (go to bed), sleep like a log (sleep deeply), burn the midnight oil (work late into the night), catch forty winks (take a short nap).

• Other "hit" idioms: hit the road (start a journey), hit the nail on the head (be exactly right), hit the roof (become very angry).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A group of ants
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Colony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard collective noun for ants is a colony of ants. (चींटियों की बस्ती/समूह)

◦ A colony also serves for other social insects — a colony of bees, a colony of termites.

◦ Correct: A colony of ants had built its nest under the stone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bushel" is a unit of dry measure, also used as *a bushel of corn/apples*, not for insects.

• Option 2 "Pack" is used for a pack of wolves/dogs/cards.

• Option 4 "Comb" refers to a honeycomb, the wax structure bees build — not a group of ants.

NOTE

• Common collective nouns: a swarm of bees, a flock of sheep/birds, a herd of cattle, a school/shoal of fish, a pride of lions, a litter of puppies, a galaxy of stars.

• A nest/army of ants is also accepted in some usage lists, but SSC keys usually take colony.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

In the summer, the bear eaten a lot of berries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. eats a lot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states a habitual, general fact, so it needs the simple present tense. (सामान्य वर्तमान काल)

◦ The subject the bear is third person singular, so the verb takes -s: *eats*.

◦ Correct: In the summer, the bear eats a lot of berries.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong — "eaten" is a past participle (V3) and cannot stand alone as the main verb without an auxiliary.

• Option 2 "eat a lot" fails subject–verb agreement; a singular subject cannot take the plain plural form.

• Option 3 "have ate a lot" is doubly wrong: "have" does not agree with the singular subject, and after have/has the correct form is eaten, not "ate".

NOTE

• Simple present rule: with he/she/it or a singular noun, add -s/-es; with I/we/you/they use the base form.

• Forms: eat – ate – eaten; use "has/have eaten" for the present perfect.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: Price is the monetery vallue placed on a product.
option_2: Price is the monetary value placed on a product.
option_3: Price is the monetary value plased on a product.
option_4: Price is the monitary value placed on a product.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Price is the monetary value placed on a product.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spellings are monetary (relating to money — मौद्रिक) and placed.

◦ "Monetary" comes from Latin *moneta* (mint/money) and is spelt m-o-n-e-t-a-r-y.

◦ Correct: Price is the monetary value placed on a product.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 has two errors — "monetery" (–ery instead of –ary) and "vallue" (double l) instead of value.

• Option 3 misspells "placed" as "plased".

• Option 4 misspells the word as "monitary" (confusing it with "monitor").

NOTE

• Words ending in -ary: monetary, secretary, necessary, temporary, voluntary, complimentary.

• Frequently misspelt SSC words: occurrence, committee, accommodation, maintenance, privilege, separate.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

There is not one/ that have not/ been duplicated.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. that have not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a relative clause the verb agrees with the antecedent of the relative pronoun. Here "that" refers back to the singular one, so the verb must be has, not "have". (कर्ता–क्रिया मेल)

◦ Rule: *one that has*, *ones that have*.

◦ Correct: There is not one that has not been duplicated.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "There is not one" is correct — the singular "is" agrees with the singular "one" in the there-construction.

• Option 4 "been duplicated." is correct — the passive present perfect needs been + V3.

• Option 1 is wrong because the sentence does contain an agreement error.

NOTE

• "One of the + plural noun + who/that + plural verb": *He is one of the boys who were selected.*

• But "the only one of the + plural noun" takes a singular verb: *He is the only one of the boys who was selected.*

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

She couldn't really be irritated with him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. annoyed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Irritated means made slightly angry or impatient. (चिढ़ा हुआ / नाराज़)

◦ Annoyed carries exactly the same sense — mildly angry or vexed — and is its closest synonym.

◦ Correct: She couldn't really be annoyed with him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "pleased" (प्रसन्न) means happy or satisfied — an antonym.

• Option 2 "delighted" (आनंदित) means greatly pleased — also an antonym.

• Option 4 "obliged" (आभारी) means grateful or bound to do something — unrelated to anger.

NOTE

• Synonyms of irritated: vexed, exasperated, peeved, nettled, riled, aggravated.

• Antonyms of irritated: calm, soothed, pacified, contented, pleased.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

He bought (a baker's dozen) of biscuits.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Thirteen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom a baker's dozen means thirteen — one more than an ordinary dozen. (तेरह)

◦ Historically bakers added an extra loaf to every twelve so as not to fall short of the legal weight and face a penalty.

◦ Correct: He bought a baker's dozen (thirteen) of biscuits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Twelve" is a plain dozen, which is precisely what the idiom exceeds by one.

• Option 3 "Fifteen" has no connection with the idiom.

• Option 4 "Ten" is a decade in counting, not a baker's dozen.

NOTE

• Number idioms: at sixes and sevens (in confusion), a nine days' wonder (short-lived sensation), the eleventh hour (the last possible moment), second to none (the best).

• A gross = 12 dozen = 144; a score = 20.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The event, promised to be a grand show, will see a display of grit, ______ and mettle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. zeal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Zeal means great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause. (उत्साह / जोश)

◦ The blank sits in a list with grit (courage/determination) and mettle (spirit, ability to face difficulty), so a noun naming a similar quality of character is needed — zeal.

◦ Correct: The event ... will see a display of grit, zeal and mettle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tyro" (नवसिखिया) means a beginner or novice — a person, not a quality.

• Option 3 "umbrage" (नाराज़गी) means offence or resentment, which is negative and out of place.

• Option 4 "zenith" (शिखर) means the highest point, a position rather than a personal quality.

NOTE

• Synonyms of zeal: fervour, ardour, passion, gusto, verve.

• Useful pairs: mettle = courage/spirit; metal = the substance. "To show one's mettle" = to prove one's courage.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

Our children need vital lessons in wealth management.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. superfluous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vital means absolutely necessary, essential. (अत्यंत आवश्यक)

◦ Superfluous means unnecessary, more than is needed — the exact opposite of essential. (अनावश्यक / अतिरिक्त)

◦ Correct: Our children need superfluous lessons in wealth management. (as the antonym substitution)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "clever" (चतुर) means quick-witted — not an opposite of "vital".

• Option 3 "organic" (जैविक) relates to living matter or chemical-free produce.

• Option 4 "healthy" (स्वस्थ) is closer to another sense of "vital" (full of life), so it is nearer a synonym than an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vital: crucial, indispensable, imperative, pivotal, cardinal.

• Synonyms of superfluous: redundant, surplus, needless, excess, gratuitous.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

The symbols were useless to him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. worthless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Useless means of no use, serving no purpose. (बेकार / निरर्थक)

◦ Worthless means having no value or usefulness — the closest synonym among the options.

◦ Correct: The symbols were worthless to him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "reachable" (पहुँच योग्य) means able to be reached or contacted — unrelated to usefulness.

• Option 2 "valuable" (मूल्यवान) is an antonym — it means of great worth.

• Option 4 "successful" (सफल) describes achieving an aim, again the opposite direction of meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of useless: futile, fruitless, ineffective, vain, unavailing.

• Antonyms of useless: useful, beneficial, effective, productive, worthwhile.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Plagiarism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is P-l-a-g-i-a-r-i-s-m.

◦ Plagiarism means the act of passing off another person's writing or ideas as one's own. (साहित्यिक चोरी)

◦ Correct: The student was penalised for plagiarism in his research paper.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Plageriasm" wrongly uses "ger" and reverses the letters to "iasm".

• Option 2 "Plagerism" replaces the "gia" with "ger".

• Option 4 "Plagiarsm" drops the "i" before "sm".

NOTE

• Word family: plagiarise (verb), plagiarist (the person), plagiarism (the act).

• It comes from Latin *plagiarius* meaning "kidnapper".

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A person, who travels in spacecraft
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Astronaut.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An astronaut is a person trained to travel in a spacecraft. (अंतरिक्ष यात्री)

◦ The word comes from Greek *astron* (star) + *nautes* (sailor) — literally a "star sailor".

◦ Correct: Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian astronaut to travel in space.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Ghetto" is a poor, crowded area of a city inhabited by a minority group — a place, not a person.

• Option 2 "Cadet" is a trainee in the armed forces or police.

• Option 3 "Voyeur" is a person who gains pleasure from secretly watching others.

NOTE

• Regional equivalents: cosmonaut (Russia), taikonaut (China), astronaut (USA/general), vyomanaut/gaganaut (India — Gaganyaan).

• Related one-word substitutions: aeronaut (balloon/airship traveller), navigator (one who plots a course), somnambulist (sleepwalker).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate choice.

His students from his time at Manchester University remember his lectures as extraordinarily ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. lucid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lucid means clear, easy to understand, expressed plainly. (स्पष्ट / सुबोध)

◦ Lectures remembered fondly by students would be praised for clarity, so "extraordinarily lucid" fits perfectly.

◦ Correct: ... remember his lectures as extraordinarily lucid.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rancid" (बासी/सड़ा) describes fat or oil that has gone stale and smells unpleasant.

• Option 2 "ballistic" refers to projectiles; idiomatically "go ballistic" means to become furious — not a quality of lectures.

• Option 3 "flaccid" (ढीला) means soft and limp, or lacking vigour — a negative sense that clashes with "remember" approvingly.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lucid: coherent, intelligible, perspicuous, transparent, comprehensible.

• Antonyms of lucid: obscure, vague, confusing, muddled, unintelligible.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

(Hardly had I started mowing the lawn that) it started raining.
option_1: No sooner did I started mowing the lawn than
option_2: Hardly had I started mowing the lawn when
option_4: Hardly did I start mowing the lawn than
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hardly had I started mowing the lawn when.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correlative pair is hardly/scarcely ... when/before, while no sooner pairs with than. (सहसंबंधी युग्म)

◦ After an initial "Hardly", the clause is inverted and takes the past perfect: *Hardly had + subject + V3*.

◦ Correct: Hardly had I started mowing the lawn when it started raining.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong twice over — after the inverted auxiliary "did" the base form "start" is required, not "started".

• Option 3 is wrong because the printed "Hardly ... that" is an incorrect pairing and must be substituted.

• Option 4 wrongly joins "Hardly" with "than" and uses the simple past instead of the past perfect.

NOTE

• Fixed pairs: no sooner ... than, hardly ... when/before, scarcely ... when/before, barely ... when.

• Inversion after negative openers: *Never had I seen*, *Seldom does he speak*, *Rarely do we meet*.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

If you want to have two cats, a male and a female will usually gotten along.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. will usually get.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the modal will, the verb must be in its bare infinitive (V1) form — *will get*, never "will gotten" or "will got". (मॉडल के बाद V1)

◦ The adverb usually correctly modifies the verb; the adjective "usual" cannot.

◦ Correct: If you want to have two cats, a male and a female will usually get along.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "will usual get" wrongly uses the adjective "usual" where the adverb "usually" is needed.

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because "will ... gotten" (modal + V3) is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 "will usually got" places the past form V2 after a modal, which is not allowed.

NOTE

• Modals (will, shall, can, may, must, should, would, could, might) are always followed by V1.

• Get along (with) = to have a friendly relationship. Other phrasal verbs: *get over* (recover), *get by* (manage), *get across* (communicate).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each went his way, the prince to (1) ______ the ways of the court, the brahmin to (2) ______ with Parasuram, the renowned scholar-warrior. He mastered (3) ______, married a virtuous woman, and (4) ______ a beautiful son. (5) ______ poor, he was proud of his learning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. learn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The prince went away to learn the ways of the court — to acquire knowledge or skill through study and practice. (सीखना)

◦ "Learn" collocates naturally with "the ways of", matching the parallel clause about the brahmin going to study with Parasuram.

◦ Correct: Each went his way, the prince to learn the ways of the court ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "absorb" means to soak up or take in gradually; "absorb the ways of the court" is not idiomatic here.

• Option 2 "receive" means to be given something — ways of the court are not "received".

• Option 3 "cram" means to memorise hurriedly for an examination, a sense that does not suit courtly training.

NOTE

• Learn = to gain knowledge; teach = to impart it. Forms: learn – learnt/learned – learnt/learned.

• Collocations: learn a lesson, learn by heart, learn the ropes (to learn how a job is done).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each went his way, the prince to (1) ______ the ways of the court, the brahmin to (2) ______ with Parasuram, the renowned scholar-warrior. He mastered (3) ______, married a virtuous woman, and (4) ______ a beautiful son. (5) ______ poor, he was proud of his learning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. study further.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Further here is an adverb meaning "to a greater extent / more", so study further = to continue one's studies to a higher level. (आगे अध्ययन करना)

◦ The brahmin goes to study further with Parasuram, the renowned scholar-warrior — advanced learning under a great teacher.

◦ Correct: ... the brahmin to study further with Parasuram, the renowned scholar-warrior.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "study across" is not an English collocation.

• Option 2 "study former" is ungrammatical — "former" is an adjective needing a noun.

• Option 3 "study another" is incomplete; "another" is a determiner that must be followed by a singular noun.

NOTE

• Further (extent/additional) vs farther (physical distance): *for further information* / *he walked farther*.

• Similar adverb collocations: read further, enquire further, look further into the matter.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each went his way, the prince to (1) ______ the ways of the court, the brahmin to (2) ______ with Parasuram, the renowned scholar-warrior. He mastered (3) ______, married a virtuous woman, and (4) ______ a beautiful son. (5) ______ poor, he was proud of his learning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
option_2: the art even craft of war
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the arts of war.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The arts of war is the standard expression for the skills and techniques of warfare. (युद्ध कला)

◦ It follows the verb mastered, which collocates with a body of skills — *he mastered the arts of war*.

◦ Correct: He mastered the arts of war, married a virtuous woman ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the supplies of war" refers to materials/provisions, which one does not "master".

• Option 2 "the art even craft of war" is ungrammatical — "even" cannot join two nouns; "and" would be needed.

• Option 3 "the attitude of war" is meaningless in this context; an attitude is a mindset, not something mastered under a teacher.

NOTE

• Collocations with master: master a language, master a skill, master the technique.

• Sun Tzu's classic treatise is titled *The Art of War*.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each went his way, the prince to (1) ______ the ways of the court, the brahmin to (2) ______ with Parasuram, the renowned scholar-warrior. He mastered (3) ______, married a virtuous woman, and (4) ______ a beautiful son. (5) ______ poor, he was proud of his learning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. had.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is narrated in the simple past tense — *went, mastered, married* — so the verb in the blank must also be past: had. (सामान्य भूतकाल)

◦ The three verbs are joined by "and" in a parallel series, so all must share the same tense form.

◦ Correct: He mastered the arts of war, married a virtuous woman, and had a beautiful son.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "has" is present tense and breaks the parallelism with "mastered" and "married".

• Option 3 "have" is the plain present form, also wrong in tense.

• Option 4 "given" is a past participle (V3) which cannot stand alone without an auxiliary such as "was/had".

NOTE

• Parallelism rule: items joined by and/or must be in the same grammatical form — *He came, saw and conquered*.

• "Have a son/daughter" = to become a parent; "had a son" is the standard past form.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Each went his way, the prince to (1) ______ the ways of the court, the brahmin to (2) ______ with Parasuram, the renowned scholar-warrior. He mastered (3) ______, married a virtuous woman, and (4) ______ a beautiful son. (5) ______ poor, he was proud of his learning.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Though.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Though is a subordinating conjunction showing contrast/concession — "in spite of the fact that". (यद्यपि / हालाँकि)

◦ There is a clear contrast between being poor and being proud of his learning, so a concessive linker is required.

◦ Correct: Though poor, he was proud of his learning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "So" expresses result, but poverty is not the cause of his pride.

• Option 2 "Even" is an adverb of emphasis; the concessive form would have to be "even though", not "even" alone.

• Option 4 "Because" expresses reason, giving an illogical sense — he was not proud on account of being poor.

NOTE

• Concession linkers: though, although, even though, even if, while, whereas, despite/in spite of + noun/gerund.

• "Though" can be reduced before an adjective: *Though (he was) poor, he was proud.*

question: The terms Kumi-Kata, Shintai, Ukemi are associated with which sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Judo.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kumi-kata (gripping the opponent's judogi), Shintai (advancing and retreating body movement) and Ukemi (the art of break-falling safely) are all standard Judo terms. (जूडो)

• Judo was founded by Jigoro Kano in Japan in 1882; it became an Olympic sport for men at Tokyo 1964 and for women at Barcelona 1992.

• Other Judo terms: Ippon (full point), Waza-ari, Dojo (practice hall), Judoka (player), Tatami (mat), Randori (free practice).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fencing terms: Foil, Epee, Sabre, Riposte, Lunge, Piste.

• Wrestling terms: Half Nelson, Takedown, Freestyle, Greco-Roman, Pin/Fall.

• Polo terms: Chukker, Mallet, Bunker, Ride-off; India's Indian Polo Association governs the sport.

NOTE

• Indian Judo achievements: Sushila Devi Likmabam won silver at the 2014 Commonwealth Games and Tulika Maan won silver at Birmingham 2022.

• Judo's governing body is the International Judo Federation (IJF), founded in 1951, headquartered in Budapest, Hungary.

question: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 declares the instant divorce granted by pronouncement of talaq three times as void and illegal. It provides for imprisonment for a term up to ______ and fine to the husband who practiced instant Triple Talaq.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 makes the pronouncement of instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) void and illegal, punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine. (तीन तलाक अधिनियम, 2019)

• The offence is cognizable and non-bailable, but an FIR can be lodged only by the wife or her blood relatives / relatives by marriage.

• The Act entitles the woman to a subsistence allowance and custody of her minor children.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Act followed the Supreme Court's judgment in Shayara Bano v. Union of India (August 2017), which struck down instant triple talaq by a 3:2 majority.

• The Bill was passed by Parliament in July 2019 and given retrospective effect from 19 September 2018.

• Other social-reform laws: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006; Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

NOTE

• Forms of talaq: Talaq-e-Ahsan (most approved), Talaq-e-Hasan (approved) and Talaq-e-Biddat (instant, now banned).

• Related constitutional articles: Article 14 (equality), Article 15 (non-discrimination) and Article 21 (life and personal liberty).

question: Which of the following is celebrated as birth anniversary of Gautama Buddha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vesak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vesak, known in India as Buddha Purnima or Buddha Jayanti, marks the birth of Gautama Buddha; it also commemorates his enlightenment and Mahaparinirvana, all believed to have occurred on the same full-moon day. (वैशाख पूर्णिमा / बुद्ध जयंती)

• It falls on the full moon day of the month of Vaisakha (April–May).

• The United Nations recognised Vesak as an international observance day in 1999.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Maha Shivaratri — festival dedicated to Lord Shiva, on the 14th night of the dark fortnight of Phalguna/Magha.

• Pongal — a four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu celebrated in January (Thai month).

• Holika Dahan — the bonfire ritual on the eve of Holi, marking the burning of Holika.

NOTE

• Buddha was born at Lumbini (Nepal), attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Bihar), gave his first sermon at Sarnath (Varanasi) and died at Kushinagar (Uttar Pradesh).

• Other Buddhist festivals: Asalha Puja (Dhamma Day), Losar, Hemis festival (Ladakh).

question: 'Romancing with Life' is an autobiography of the evergreen star ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dev Anand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Romancing with Life’ (2007) is the autobiography of the legendary Hindi film actor-producer-director Dev Anand, released on his 84th birthday. (देव आनंद की आत्मकथा)

• Dev Anand (1923–2011), the ‘evergreen star’, founded the production house Navketan Films (1949) with his brother Chetan Anand.

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan (2001) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2002).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dilip Kumar's autobiography is ‘The Substance and the Shadow’ (2014).

• Shashi Kapoor is the subject of the biography ‘Shashi Kapoor: The Householder, The Star’ by Aseem Chhabra.

• Kishore Kumar was a legendary playback singer-actor; a well-known biography on him is ‘Kishore Kumar: The Ultimate Biography’.

NOTE

• Famous Indian autobiographies: ‘My Experiments with Truth’ — Mahatma Gandhi; ‘Wings of Fire’ — A.P.J. Abdul Kalam; ‘An Autobiography’ — Jawaharlal Nehru; ‘Playing It My Way’ — Sachin Tendulkar; ‘Unbreakable’ — Mary Kom.

• Dev Anand's famous films: Guide, Jewel Thief, Hare Rama Hare Krishna, CID, Kala Pani.

question: Minal wrote an essay on the largest moon of Saturn. Which among the following moons is it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Titan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Titan is the largest moon of Saturn and the second largest moon in the Solar System after Jupiter's Ganymede. (शनि का सबसे बड़ा उपग्रह)

• It was discovered by the Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens in 1655.

• Titan is the only moon known to have a dense nitrogen-rich atmosphere and stable surface lakes of liquid methane and ethane.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Atlas is a small inner ‘shepherd’ moon of Saturn discovered from Voyager 1 images (1980).

• Carme is a small irregular retrograde moon of Jupiter, discovered in 1938.

• Europa is one of the four Galilean moons of Jupiter, believed to have a subsurface ocean beneath its icy crust.

NOTE

• Largest moons of planets: Earth — Moon, Mars — Phobos, Jupiter — Ganymede, Saturn — Titan, Uranus — Titania, Neptune — Triton.

• The Cassini–Huygens mission (NASA–ESA–ASI) reached Saturn in 2004; the Huygens probe landed on Titan in January 2005.

question: FIFA World Cup is associated with _____ sport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Football.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The FIFA World Cup is the premier international football (soccer) tournament, held every four years. (फुटबॉल विश्व कप)

• FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland.

• The first World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930; the 2022 edition in Qatar was won by Argentina, who beat France on penalties, with Lionel Messi winning the Golden Ball.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Hockey — governed by the FIH; the Hockey World Cup 2023 was hosted by India (Odisha) and won by Germany.

• Fencing — an Olympic sword-fighting sport governed by the FIE; Bhavani Devi was the first Indian fencer to qualify for the Olympics (Tokyo 2020).

• Rugby — the Rugby World Cup is organised by World Rugby; the 2023 edition in France was won by South Africa.

NOTE

• Football trophies: FIFA World Cup, Ballon d'Or, Santosh Trophy, Durand Cup (Asia's oldest football tournament, started 1888), Subroto Cup, Duleep Trophy is cricket, not football.

• Brazil has won the most FIFA World Cup titles — five (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Mass Media?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Door to door campaign.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mass media refers to channels that convey information to a very large, scattered audience simultaneously — radio, television, newspapers, magazines, cinema and the internet. (जनसंचार माध्यम)

• A door-to-door campaign is a form of interpersonal / direct communication with individuals or small groups, not mass communication.

• Mass media requires technology and a mass audience; personal canvassing lacks both.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Radio — India's first radio broadcast was in 1923 (Radio Club of Bombay); All India Radio (AIR) was named so in 1936.

• Television — Doordarshan began experimental telecast on 15 September 1959 and became a separate entity in 1976.

• Newspapers — India's first newspaper was ‘Bengal Gazette’ (1780) by James Augustus Hicky.

NOTE

• Types of media: Print media (newspapers, magazines), Electronic/broadcast media (radio, TV), New media (internet, social media).

• The Press Council of India (statutory, 1966/1978) is the watchdog of the press; Prasar Bharati (1997) is the public service broadcaster.

question: The last Mughal Emperor who was sent to Jail in Rangoon was ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahadur Shah Zafar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bahadur Shah Zafar (Bahadur Shah II) was the last Mughal Emperor; after the Revolt of 1857 he was tried by the British and exiled to Rangoon (Burma) in 1858, where he died in 1862. (अंतिम मुगल सम्राट)

• The rebel sepoys of Meerut marched to Delhi and proclaimed him the symbolic leader (Shahenshah-e-Hindustan) of the revolt.

• He was a noted Urdu poet who wrote under the pen name ‘Zafar’.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shah Alam II — during his reign the British won the Battle of Buxar (1764) and obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha (1765).

• Akbar Shah II (1806–1837) — he gave Raja Ram Mohan Roy the title ‘Raja’ and sent him to England.

• Alamgir II (1754–1759) — during his reign the British won the Battle of Plassey (1757).

NOTE

• Mughal rulers in order: Babur (1526) → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb (d. 1707) → ... → Bahadur Shah Zafar (1857).

• The Revolt of 1857 began at Barrackpore (Mangal Pandey, 29 March 1857) and erupted at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

question: Which of the following vitamins helps our body to use calcium for bones and teeth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitamin D.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin D (Calciferol) promotes the absorption of calcium and phosphorus from the intestine, which is essential for strong bones and teeth. (विटामिन डी — कैल्सिफेरॉल)

• It is called the ‘sunshine vitamin’ because it is synthesised in the skin on exposure to ultraviolet (UV) rays of sunlight.

• Its deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) — deficiency causes scurvy; sources: amla, citrus fruits.

• Vitamin A (Retinol) — deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia; sources: carrots, papaya, liver.

• Vitamin E (Tocopherol) — an antioxidant; deficiency causes sterility/reproductive problems.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K; water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C.

• Vitamin K (Phylloquinone) helps in blood clotting; Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin) deficiency causes pernicious anaemia; Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency causes beri-beri.

question: Which among the following dance forms of India is associated with Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau is a semi-classical masked dance associated with Odisha (Mayurbhanj Chhau), along with Jharkhand (Seraikella Chhau) and West Bengal (Purulia Chhau). (छऊ नृत्य)

• It was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Odisha's classical dance is Odissi; its folk dances include Chhau, Ghumura, Ranappa and Dalkhai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bhangra — a vigorous harvest folk dance of Punjab, performed at Baisakhi.

• Ghoomar — a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by women in swirling ghagras.

• Kathak — a classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), with Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras gharanas.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Other folk dances: Garba — Gujarat; Bihu — Assam; Lavani — Maharashtra; Yakshagana — Karnataka.

question: Which layer of the soil has maximum concentration of humus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Top soil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The top soil (A-horizon) contains the maximum humus — the dark organic matter formed by the decomposition of dead plants and animals. (ह्यूमस — जैविक पदार्थ)

• Humus makes the top soil dark in colour, fertile and rich in nutrients such as nitrogen, and improves the soil's water-holding capacity.

• The top soil supports root growth, micro-organisms and burrowing animals like earthworms.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sub soil (B-horizon) — contains more clay, iron and minerals leached down from above, with little humus.

• Weathered rock material (C-horizon) — partially broken parent rock, sometimes called regolith.

• Parent rock (R-horizon/bedrock) — unweathered solid rock at the base of the soil profile.

NOTE

• Soil profile order from top: O (organic litter) → A (top soil) → B (sub soil) → C (weathered rock) → R (bedrock).

• Major soil types of India: Alluvial (most widespread), Black (Regur, best for cotton), Red, Laterite, Desert, Mountain soils.

question: Which among the following is a tributary of river Narmada?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tawa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tawa is the largest tributary of the Narmada, rising in the Mahadeo hills of the Satpura range in Madhya Pradesh and joining the Narmada near Bandrabhan (Hoshangabad/Narmadapuram). (तवा — नर्मदा की सहायक नदी)

• The Narmada rises from Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh), flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges and falls into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).

• Other Narmada tributaries: Hiran, Burhner, Banjar, Sher, Shakkar, Orsang.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Koyna is a tributary of the Krishna river in Maharashtra; the Koyna Dam is a major hydro-power project.

• Ken and Betwa are tributaries of the Yamuna; the Ken–Betwa Link Project is India's first river-interlinking project.

• The Narmada is also called the ‘Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh’; the Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on it in Gujarat.

NOTE

• West-flowing peninsular rivers: Narmada, Tapi (Tapti), Mahi, Sabarmati, Luni.

• East-flowing peninsular rivers forming deltas: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri.

• The Dhuandhar Falls at Bhedaghat (Jabalpur) are on the Narmada, famous for its marble rocks.

question: Which part of the Indian constitution talks about the Union Territories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part VIII.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part VIII (Articles 239 to 241) of the Constitution deals with the Union Territories. (भाग VIII — संघ राज्य क्षेत्र)

• Article 239 — administration of UTs by the President through an Administrator; Article 239A — creation of local legislatures; Article 239AA — special provisions for Delhi (NCT).

• Article 240 — power of the President to make regulations for certain UTs; Article 241 — High Courts for Union Territories.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part VI (Articles 152–237) — the States (Governor, State Legislature, High Courts).

• Part X (Article 244) — the Scheduled and Tribal Areas.

• Part XI (Articles 245–263) — relations between the Union and the States (legislative and administrative).

NOTE

• India currently has 8 Union Territories; Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have legislatures.

• Other key Parts: Part III — Fundamental Rights, Part IV — DPSP, Part IVA — Fundamental Duties, Part IX — Panchayats, Part IXA — Municipalities.

question: Which among the following memoir is based on ex-Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Accidental Prime Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘The Accidental Prime Minister: The Making and Unmaking of Manmohan Singh’ (2014) is a memoir by Sanjaya Baru, who served as media adviser to Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh (2004–2008). (मनमोहन सिंह पर संस्मरण)

• A film based on the book, starring Anupam Kher as Manmohan Singh, was released in 2019.

• Dr Manmohan Singh was Prime Minister from 2004 to 2014, and earlier the Finance Minister (1991–96) who launched India's LPG economic reforms.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• ‘A Prime Minister to Remember’ is a book by Admiral Sushil Kumar on P.V. Narasimha Rao.

• ‘The Change We Choose’ is a collection of speeches by Gordon Brown, former UK Prime Minister.

• Other books on Manmohan Singh: ‘Strictly Personal: Manmohan and Gursharan’ by Daman Singh (his daughter).

NOTE

• Dr Manmohan Singh was also Governor of the RBI (1982–85) and Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

• Notable political memoirs: ‘My Country My Life’ — L.K. Advani; ‘Matoshree’ / ‘One Life Is Not Enough’ — Natwar Singh; ‘Playing to Win’ — Saina Nehwal.

question: Which famous ruler was known as the "Second Ashoka"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanishka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kanishka I, the greatest Kushana ruler (accession usually dated 78 CE), is called the ‘Second Ashoka’ for his patronage of Buddhism. (कनिष्क — द्वितीय अशोक)

• He convened the Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalvana, Kashmir, presided over by Vasumitra with Ashvaghosha as deputy, where Buddhism split into Hinayana and Mahayana.

• He is believed to have started the Saka Era in 78 CE, which is India's national calendar; his capital was Purushapura (Peshawar).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) — Gupta ruler in whose court the Navaratnas (including Kalidasa) flourished; the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign.

• Rudradaman I — Saka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler famous for the Junagadh rock inscription, the first long inscription in chaste Sanskrit, recording repair of the Sudarshana lake.

• Milinda (Menander) — Indo-Greek king converted to Buddhism by Nagasena; their dialogue is recorded in the ‘Milinda Panha’.

NOTE

• Kanishka patronised Ashvaghosha (author of *Buddhacharita*), Charaka (physician), Nagarjuna and Vasumitra.

• Art schools of the Kushana period: Gandhara school (Greco-Roman influence) and Mathura school (indigenous, red sandstone).

question: The Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Hardeep Singh Puri, in October 2022 inaugurated Asia's largest Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) plant in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2022, Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri inaugurated Asia's largest Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) plant at Lehragaga, Sangrur district, Punjab. (पंजाब — एशिया का सबसे बड़ा सीबीजी संयंत्र)

• The plant uses paddy straw (parali) as feedstock, helping curb stubble burning and air pollution in North India.

• It was set up under the SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) initiative launched in 2018.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) is produced from agricultural residue, cattle dung and municipal solid waste; it has methane content of over 90% and is a substitute for CNG.

• Hardeep Singh Puri holds the portfolios of Petroleum & Natural Gas and Housing & Urban Affairs.

• Related schemes: GOBAR-Dhan Yojana (2018), National Bio-Energy Programme, National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023).

NOTE

• Punjab: capital Chandigarh (shared with Haryana), rivers Sutlej, Beas, Ravi; known as the ‘Granary of India’.

• India targets 20% ethanol blending in petrol by 2025-26, advanced from the earlier 2030 target.

question: All human beings have ______ pairs of chromosomes in the nuclei of their cells.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 23.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Human body (somatic) cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes, i.e. 46 chromosomes in the nucleus. (गुणसूत्र — 23 जोड़े)

• Of these, 22 pairs are autosomes and 1 pair is the sex chromosomes — XX in females and XY in males.

• The father's sperm determines the sex of the child, since it may carry either an X or a Y chromosome, while the ovum always carries X.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chromosomes are made of DNA and histone proteins; the term ‘chromosome’ was coined by W. Waldeyer (1888).

• Gametes (sperm and egg) are haploid (n = 23); fertilisation restores the diploid (2n = 46) number.

• Chromosomal disorders: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (XO), Klinefelter syndrome (XXY).

NOTE

• Chromosome numbers: Human — 46, Pea — 14, Onion — 16, Rice — 24, Dog — 78, Housefly — 12.

• The Human Genome Project was completed in 2003; DNA's double-helix structure was proposed by Watson and Crick (1953).

question: Islamic style of architecture is also known as _____ style.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mehrab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Islamic (Indo-Islamic) style of architecture is also referred to as the Mehrab (Mihrab) style, named after the mihrab — the arched niche in a mosque wall that indicates the qibla, the direction of Mecca. (मेहराब शैली)

• The style is arcuate — based on arches, domes, minarets and vaults — as against the indigenous trabeate (post-and-lintel) Hindu style.

• Materials and features include lime mortar, calligraphy, arabesque, jaali work and pietra dura.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Hegira (Hijra) — the migration of Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE, the starting point of the Islamic calendar.

• Yashmak — a type of veil worn by women in some Islamic societies; not an architectural term.

• Alim (Ulema) — a learned scholar of Islamic law and theology.

NOTE

• Indo-Islamic architectural schools: Delhi (Imperial), Provincial (Bengal, Jaunpur, Malwa, Gujarat, Bijapur) and Mughal.

• Landmark structures: Qutub Minar and Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque (Qutb-ud-din Aibak), Alai Darwaza (Alauddin Khilji), Taj Mahal and Jama Masjid (Shah Jahan), Gol Gumbaz, Bijapur (Muhammad Adil Shah).

question: Which among the following is a noble chemical element of science periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Helium (He, atomic number 2) is a noble (inert) gas belonging to Group 18 of the modern periodic table. (उत्कृष्ट गैस — हीलियम)

• Noble gases have completely filled outermost shells (duplet in He, octet in others), which makes them chemically inert and monatomic.

• Helium is the second most abundant element in the universe and the second lightest; it is used to fill balloons and airships, in cryogenics, and in oxygen-helium mixtures for divers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nitrogen (N, 7) — a Group 15 non-metal that forms about 78% of the atmosphere; it is inert-like but not a noble gas.

• Scandium (Sc, 21) — the first transition (d-block) element.

• Cobalt (Co, 27) — a transition metal; it is the central metal atom of Vitamin B12.

NOTE

• The noble gases are Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), Radon (Rn) and Oganesson (Og).

• Uses: Neon — advertising signs; Argon — filling electric bulbs and welding; Radon — radioactive, used in cancer treatment.

• The modern periodic table is based on Moseley's periodic law (1913) — properties are a periodic function of atomic number.

question: Which of the following tribe belongs to Indo-European Linguistic family?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhili.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhili, the language of the Bhil tribe, belongs to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European (Indo-Germanic) language family. (भीली — भारोपीय परिवार)

• The Bhils are one of India's largest tribes, spread across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra.

• The Indo-European (Indo-Aryan) family covers about 73% of India's population and includes Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Punjabi, Assamese and Bhili.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Garo — spoken by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya; belongs to the Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman) family.

• Gondi — spoken by the Gond tribe of central India; belongs to the Dravidian family.

• Korwa — spoken by the Korwa tribe of Jharkhand/Chhattisgarh; belongs to the Austro-Asiatic (Munda) family.

NOTE

• India's four language families: Indo-European (Indo-Aryan), Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic (Austric) and Sino-Tibetan.

• Bhil folk art: Pithora painting; Bhil festivals: Bhagoria and Ghoomar; the Bhils are known as the ‘bowmen of Rajasthan’.

question: When was the Battle of Talikota fought?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1565.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Talikota was fought in 1565 between the Vijayanagara Empire and the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates — Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar. (तालीकोट का युद्ध, 1565)

• The Vijayanagara army was led by Rama Raya (regent of the Aravidu dynasty), who was defeated and killed; the capital Hampi was sacked.

• The battle marked the effective decline of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1556 — the Second Battle of Panipat, in which Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan defeated Hemu.

• 1576 — the Battle of Haldighati between Maharana Pratap and Akbar's army led by Man Singh.

• Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529) was the greatest Vijayanagara ruler; he wrote ‘Amuktamalyada’ in Telugu.

NOTE

• Vijayanagara dynasties in order: Sangama → Saluva → Tuluva → Aravidu.

• Hampi (Karnataka), the ruined capital, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986); foreign travellers Domingo Paes, Nuniz, Abdur Razzaq and Nicolo Conti visited Vijayanagara.

question: How many types of revenue receipts exist in the economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Two.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Revenue receipts of the government are of two types — Tax revenue and Non-tax revenue. (राजस्व प्राप्तियाँ — दो प्रकार)

• Revenue receipts are those receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce any asset of the government.

• Tax revenue includes direct taxes (income tax, corporation tax) and indirect taxes (GST, customs duty, excise duty).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Non-tax revenue includes interest receipts, dividends and profits from PSUs, fees, fines, and grants.

• Capital receipts either create a liability (borrowings) or reduce assets (disinvestment, recovery of loans).

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts; Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts excluding borrowings.

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 as the Annual Financial Statement, on 1 February since 2017.

• GST was implemented on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016; the GST Council is set up under Article 279A.

question: According to the 2011 census, the sex ratio for India's population is _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 943.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, the sex ratio was 943 females per 1,000 males, up from 933 in 2001. (लिंगानुपात — 943)

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) fell to 919, the lowest since Independence.

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1084) and Haryana the lowest (879) among states; among UTs, Puducherry was highest (1037) and Daman & Diu lowest (618).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census and the 7th after Independence; its motto was ‘Our Census, Our Future’.

• India's population in 2011 was 121.09 crore; literacy rate 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%); density 382 persons/sq km.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala (93.91%); lowest — Bihar (61.8%).

NOTE

• The first census in India was held in 1872 under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

• Related schemes: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015) and the PCPNDT Act, 1994 against sex determination.

question: Who administers the Union Territories of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 239, every Union Territory is administered by the President acting through an Administrator appointed by him. (राष्ट्रपति — संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों का प्रशासन)

• The Administrator may be designated a Lieutenant Governor, Chief Commissioner or Administrator; the Governor of a neighbouring State may also be appointed as Administrator.

• The Administrator is an agent of the President, not a constitutional head like a State Governor.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have their own legislative assemblies and Councils of Ministers, but the Lt. Governor retains wide powers.

• Parliament can make laws for any subject (including State List) for the Union Territories.

• The President can make regulations for Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, and Ladakh under Article 240.

NOTE

• India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories; Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir became UTs on 31 October 2019.

• Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu were merged into a single UT on 26 January 2020.

question: Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non – cooperation Movement in February 1922 after which incident?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chauri Chaura Incident.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 5 February 1922, an agitated mob at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, United Provinces (Uttar Pradesh), set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. (चौरी चौरा कांड)

• Shocked by the violence, Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12 February 1922 at the Bardoli session of the Congress Working Committee.

• The Non-Cooperation Movement had been launched in 1920 (Nagpur session) along with the Khilafat Movement, on the principle of non-violent non-cooperation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Central Legislative Assembly bomb blast (8 April 1929) — by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt, protesting the Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill.

• Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (13 April 1919) — General Dyer ordered firing at Amritsar; Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest.

• Kakori train robbery (9 August 1925) — by the HRA (Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Rajendra Lahiri, Roshan Singh).

NOTE

• Gandhi's three major mass movements: Non-Cooperation (1920–22), Civil Disobedience (1930–34, Dandi March) and Quit India (1942, ‘Do or Die’).

• After the withdrawal, C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party (1923) to enter legislatures.
